paragraphs.source_en: By the fifth year of Keichō, the rewards and punishments following the Battle of Sekigahara had largely been settled; only part of the Uesugi domain in Ōu and the Shimazu clan of Kyūshū remained. Ieyasu had long since decided how he would deal with the lords of both houses.

paragraphs.source_en: “It seems I may rest a little easier now!” Ieyasu sighed, then summoned Fujiwara Seika and devoted himself to hearing lectures on the Book of Han and the other works of the Seventeen Histories.

paragraphs.source_zh: “似乎稍稍心安矣！”家康叹道，随即叫来藤原惺窝，专心致志地听他讲授《汉书》等十七史。

paragraphs.source_en: The maker of a new age could never afford to relax merely because the realm had just been pacified; the late Taikō offered the finest warning. The perils of the age of war had bred a bellicose habit in men, who resorted to force at the slightest provocation. Beyond doubt, that habit still lingered in the hearts of the people of this time. But how was it to be purged?

units.source_en: The maker of a new age could never afford to relax merely because the realm had just been pacified; the late Taikō offered the finest warning.

units.source_en: The perils of the age of war had bred a bellicose habit in men, who resorted to force at the slightest provocation.

units.source_en: But how was it to be purged?

paragraphs.source_zh: 时代的缔造者，绝不可因天下初定而稍有松懈，已故太阁便是极好的例子。乱世的艰险养就了世人好战的习性，人们动辄诉诸武力。毋庸置疑，这种习性依然残留于此际世人心中。但当如何清除这种习性？

paragraphs.source_en: Taking this as an auspicious sign, Ieyasu swiftly turned to another vital undertaking besides learning: a policy for enriching the realm. Without a prosperous realm, how could peace be preserved? Wealth, learning, and arms formed the three great pillars supporting an age of peace and prosperity. At the seven-day celebration held in the Western Enclosure for Ieyasu’s seventh son, Gorōtamaru, Ōkubo Tadachika brought with him a remarkable man—one who could help Ieyasu accomplish this great undertaking.

units.source_en: At the seven-day celebration held in the Western Enclosure for Ieyasu’s seventh son, Gorōtamaru, Ōkubo Tadachika brought with him a remarkable man—one who could help Ieyasu accomplish this great undertaking.

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu gave a great banquet for his trusted retainers in the Western Enclosure, with Noh and kyōgen performances, both to celebrate Gorōtamaru’s birth and to entertain his mother, Dentsū-in, now past seventy. Yet even seated directly before the stage, Ieyasu could never quite fix his attention upon it. “How unpredictable life truly is.” As he looked at the swaddled infant and his aged mother watching the Noh and kyōgen while nodding off, Ieyasu was overcome by emotion.

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu had no particular recollection of him, yet he was indeed so strikingly handsome that one meeting would suffice to remember him for life.
